late: Assessment Handbook — Late Submission and Illness. This synthetic teaching document is not an actual university policy. Students should read the complete clause and retain the document identifier when asking the help desk for guidance. Late submission is normally penalized according to the assessment schedule. Illness extensions require medical evidence before the deadline. A student should contact the course coordinator as soon as the illness affects planned submission. The request should identify the affected assessment and the date on which the student expects to submit. Medical evidence must relate to the relevant period and should be provided through the approved academic channel. A request does not automatically guarantee an extension; the responsible academic office reviews the evidence and communicates its decision. Students should continue preparing their work while a request is under review, unless the coordinator advises otherwise. The normal submission route is the learning portal, and the uploaded file should be checked after submission. A receipt or confirmation screen should be retained. If the portal is unavailable, the student should record the time of the problem and contact technical support. Do not assume that an email attachment counts as a successful portal submission. This document is synthetic and illustrates retrieval of a rule together with its exception. Its dates, conditions and procedures are examples only. Always consult the current official handbook for real decisions.
password: IT Help Guide — Account Recovery. This synthetic guide is instructional sample data and does not describe a real university service. Users should protect passwords and recovery codes. Reset a forgotten password using the recovery link on the login page. The recovery link may require the registered email address and an additional verification step. A user who no longer controls the registered email should contact the help desk rather than repeatedly submitting guesses. Never share a one-time code, password or recovery code with another person. Support staff should not ask users to disclose a current password. After resetting a password, sign in again and review active sessions if that option is available. If a device remains signed in unexpectedly, revoke its session through the account security page or ask support for help. A locked account may require identity verification before access is restored. Wait for the stated lockout period instead of using scripts to generate repeated attempts. If the recovery link has expired, request a new link from the official sign-in page. Do not use links received from unknown senders. This sample guide is deliberately limited; it is not a substitute for an institution's current security instructions. Report suspected account compromise promptly and include the approximate time and affected service, but never include secret credentials in a report.
assignment: Learning Portal Guide — Assignment Upload. This synthetic document demonstrates source-aware retrieval and is not a live university rule. Assignments are uploaded through the learning portal. Submit the final file as a PDF. Before uploading, confirm that the file opens correctly and that the filename identifies the assessment without exposing unnecessary personal information. Select the correct course and assessment item because similar titles may appear in different modules. Wait until the upload progress finishes and check that a submission receipt or confirmation is displayed. If the portal reports an error, save the message and contact technical support with the course code, assessment title and approximate time. Do not repeatedly upload different versions unless the assessment instructions permit resubmission. Where resubmission is allowed, check which version is marked as final. A draft saved on a personal computer is not evidence that the portal received it. A file shared through an unrelated cloud drive is not automatically a valid submission. Students should review the assessment brief for permitted file types and size limits. If the portal is unavailable near a deadline, record the outage evidence and contact the responsible support channel immediately. The course team determines how an outage affects a deadline. This teaching example contains general workflow language only; it does not establish a real institution's deadline, penalty or appeal process.
contractor: Workplace Access Policy — Contractor Remote Work. This synthetic policy is created for retrieval practice and is not legal or employment advice. Employees may request remote work with manager approval, but contractor eligibility is governed by a separate contractual condition. Contractors can work remotely only if the signed contract permits it. Employee rules do not apply to contractors. A contractor should review the signed agreement and any written amendment before arranging remote access. A verbal assumption or a colleague's practice does not change the contract. If the contract is unclear, the contractor should ask the designated contract owner for written clarification. Access to company systems must follow the approved security process regardless of work location. Remote access may require multifactor authentication and a managed device. The organisation may restrict access to sensitive systems based on role and approved project scope. A manager's general approval is not a replacement for the explicit contractual permission required in this example. Staff should not forward confidential documents to personal accounts to work around access restrictions. Any exception should be recorded by the authorised owner and linked to the applicable contract version. This synthetic example intentionally places similar employee and contractor passages in one document so that retrieval can be tested for audience conflicts. The reader must inspect the audience and condition, not select a passage only because it contains the words remote work.
printer: IT Equipment Guide — Blank Printer Pages. This synthetic troubleshooting guide is intended for classroom exercises. For blank printer pages, check ink levels and run the cleaning utility. Print a test page afterwards. Before opening a printer cover, follow the device manufacturer's safety instructions and allow hot components to cool. Confirm that the selected printer is the intended device and that the print queue does not contain a paused job. Check whether the cartridge or toner is installed correctly and whether any protective seal remains. Use the cleaning utility provided for the specific printer model; menu names differ between devices. After cleaning, print one test page and inspect whether text and images appear. If the page remains blank, stop repeating the cleaning cycle and consult the device manual or support team. A scanner producing a blank image has a different diagnostic procedure: check document placement and the selected scanning source. Do not apply printer cartridge instructions to a scanner. If a warning light appears, record its pattern and model number before requesting assistance. Avoid dismantling electrical components or using liquids not approved by the manufacturer. The steps in this synthetic guide are simplified examples, not universal instructions for every model. Device-specific manuals take priority. A technician should preserve the order of the procedure and record which checks have already been completed.
